resume: Length of the leave, notice periods for your employer, daily allowances and documents to send to the Assurance Maladie, plus the new additional birth leave.
aQuoiCaSert: Paternity and childcare leave (congé de paternité et d'accueil de l'enfant) allows the father, or the mother's spouse, PACS (civil partnership) partner or cohabiting partner, to stop working after the birth to look after the child. During this leave, the employment contract is suspended and the Assurance Maladie (French public health insurance; the CPAM, Caisse primaire d'assurance maladie, of your département) can pay daily allowances. Since July 1, 2026, an additional birth leave can be added to it.
quiEstConcerne: The mother's spouse, PACS partner or cohabiting partner, if they are not the father, and, for a female couple with joint prenatal recognition, the mother who did not give birth.
These pages concern the private sector: civil servants, self-employed people and other schemes have their own rules.
aSavoir: Separated parents: the child's father is entitled to it with no requirement of marriage, PACS or living with the mother. The requirement to live as a couple only applies to a spouse or partner who is not the father.
Length: 25 calendar days for a birth (32 for multiple births), in addition to the 3-working-day birth leave. A 4-day period is mandatory right after the birth leave.
The remaining 21 days (28 for multiple births) can be taken all at once or in 2 periods of at least 5 days, within 6 months of the birth.

Tell your employer at least 1 month before the expected date of birth, then at least 1 month before the start of each period, giving the dates and length. Doing so in writing is advised: registered letter with acknowledgment of receipt, or hand delivery against a signed receipt. The employer cannot refuse the leave.

Daily allowances: among other conditions, you must have been registered for at least 6 months and have worked 150 hours in the previous 3 months, or paid contributions on at least €12,058.20 of salary over 6 months. They range from €11.12 to €104.02 per day (service-public.gouv.fr, checked as of June 1, 2026).

Additional birth leave (congé supplémentaire de naissance; child born since January 1, 2026, in place since July 1, 2026): each parent can take 1 or 2 months after maternity or paternity leave, all at once or in two periods of one month. Employees: 70% of net salary in the 1st month, 60% in the 2nd, up to the social security ceiling. Tell the employer in writing 1 month in advance (15 days if it directly follows paternity leave).

documents.libelle: Full copy of the child's birth certificate or updated family record book (livret de famille)
documents.detail: To send to the Assurance Maladie. Certificate free on service-public.gouv.fr or from the town hall (mairie) of the place of birth.

documents.libelle: Proof of your relationship with the mother if you are not the father
documents.detail: Extract of the marriage certificate, copy of the PACS, certificate of cohabitation less than a year old, or sworn statement of living together signed by both.
Copy of the registered letter or the signed receipt, with the dates of the leave.
Sent by the employer to the Assurance Maladie. Check with them that it has been sent.
If your bank details are not up to date in your ameli account.

etapes.detail: At least 1 month before the expected date of birth, then at least 1 month before each period of leave.
Birth certificate or updated family record book, proof of relationship with the mother if you are not the father, salary statement sent by the employer, bank details and address up to date on ameli.

etapes.titre: Send the supporting documents to the Assurance Maladie
etapes.detail: In your ameli account or by post to the CPAM of your département (MSA, Mutualité sociale agricole, the farmers' social security fund, for the agricultural scheme).
Right after the 3-day birth leave paid by the employer.

etapes.titre: Plan the rest of the leave within 6 months
etapes.detail: And, if you wish, the additional birth leave: within 9 months of the birth (child born from July 1, 2026), or before March 31, 2027 (child born in the 1st half of 2026).

datesLimites.libelle: Inform the employer at least 1 month before the expected birth
datesLimites.detail: Then at least 1 month before each period.

datesLimites.libelle: Leave to be taken within 6 months of the birth
datesLimites.detail: Can be postponed in certain cases provided for by law, for example if the mother dies.

datesLimites.libelle: Additional birth leave within 9 months of the birth
datesLimites.detail: For a child born from July 1, 2026. Child born between January 1 and June 30, 2026: to be taken between July 1, 2026 and March 31, 2027 (service-public.gouv.fr).

aConfirmer: To be confirmed with your CPAM: how to send the supporting documents and how long the daily allowances take to be paid.

Additional birth leave: the Code du travail numérique page (published October 26, 2026) sets the cutoff at June 1, 2026, while service-public.gouv.fr uses July 1, 2026. For a child born in June 2026, have the deadline confirmed by your CPAM or your employer; otherwise, take the leave within 9 months of the birth.
Self-employed people and public employees: the additional birth leave follows its own rules, not detailed here.
